steps.content: [Black Screen] Or a corridor

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Are you certain about going alone? This individual is extremely dangerous. At the very least, allow me to accompany you.
If you're there, he'll never talk. I need to do this by myself.
Don't worry. You'll be right outside, right? If anything goes wrong, you can step in.
You push the door open and step into the quiet room. The door clicks shut behind you, and your eyes are drawn to the figure in the hospital bed.
[Scene Change] Hospital (Detention Cell)
It's the man you put there.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Hello, Chief. I'd nearly given up hope of seeing you again. What an unexpected pleasure.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Did you give your superiors your word not to harm me? But I heard you came this close to killing another prisoner just two days ago. Tell me, Chief, should I find comfort in such fragile promises?

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Oh, do not misunderstand. I'm perfectly at peace with dying now. Beyond disappointing my family by not bringing them gifts, my existence has become quite irrelevant to the war.
You calmly take a seat beside the bed.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Well-informed as always, you bastard. Who did you persuade to feed you information this time?

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Not quite "persuasion." Even in DisCity, there are kind souls who doubt the war, people with too many unanswered questions. Occasionally, they can't help but... "communicate" with me.
He bears fresh bruises since you last saw him, a stark testament to the "communication" others had with him.
Yet he seems utterly indifferent to them, his attention fixed on the placid stillness you now project.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: You're no different, are you?

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Your fury is so... unrestrained, Chief. It betrays how ill-prepared you were for this war. By all accounts, you should despise the very idea of war—yet here you stand, shackled to the frontlines. All for dear Hella.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I've already seen her.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Oh?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I thought finally seeing her, knowing where she was, would make me more certain. More focused.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But the truth is, it's just left me more confused than ever. I can't figure this out alone. Which is why I had no choice but to come to you. The one who started all of this.
You look down at your hands. Your palms are now a rough landscape of skin, etched with the cruel corruption of the shackles.
My whole understanding was that the Black Ring held her captive. That the Outlanders who continued to imprison and control her, even after their fall, were monsters. Bastards, like you.
I was consumed by that rage, just focused on eliminating the enemy and bringing her home. It's why I pushed that prisoner so hard.
But then... that "Hella" stopped me. And she was forceful about it.
Afterward, they told me it wasn't really her. Just a phantom, a trick of the Black Ring meant to deceive me. But I know the truth...
Hella was really there. If she wanted to deceive me, she wouldn't have let go. If she wanted me dead, she had plenty of chances before that.
She just came to see me. Used the Black Ring's power to reach me... but for what? What did she want me to do?
I don't even dream of her anymore. So I need to know... those... things that were with her, the ones that sent her... what do they want?
They must all want something, to appear to me in her form. So tell me, Sage of the Underground. What did you do with BR-005?

You lock eyes, both searching for an unspoken truth in the other's gaze. Finally, Adelaide's repulsive smile falters and vanishes. For the first time, his expression is unmasked as he answers your question.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: ...The Underground made a deal with me, only asking that I trigger BR-005 somewhere far from DisCity. I originally sought to achieve this with minimal sacrifice, but my plan failed. The Black Ring still ended up exploding.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Countless farland refugees took up the cause willingly, sacrificing themselves just for the chance of change. Even as the Black Ring consumed them, they clung to their defiant will.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: These are the vengeful spirits now haunting the Black Ring, following Hella all the way to DisCity to settle their score with fate.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Perhaps you'd still like to extend DisCity's courtesy to them. Perhaps you imagine some elaborate tale of Fraser manipulating them. But even without wartime hatreds to fuel the fire... one truth remains unchanged.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: The spread of Mania, the relentless march of calamities... the farlands have been pushed past the brink. Beyond DisCity's walls, they scrape by in the wastelands, clinging to life. And in their despair, hatred for DisCity is the only thing that keeps them going—the desperate hope that if they tear it all down, something might change.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: And yet, even consumed by such profound hatred, none have ever wished harm upon Hella.
He lowers his eyes, revealing an uncharacteristically gentle expression.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: They adore her. Even after learning her origins, they chose to protect her. She's incompatible with DisCity's sins. Everyone wants to keep her close.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: That fragile girl shows concern for Outland strangers because of her own weakness... yet never lets that weakness stop her. She makes people set aside their hatred precisely because she keeps pulling everyone toward survival, toward hope beyond despair.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: You've raised a child who shines like the sun. On behalf of many, I thank you for that.
...Don't talk like that.

steps.speaker: Option
options: It makes me want to kill you more.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: That's precisely what makes it a wasteland, where weakness itself is a sin, and those who cannot defy fate are doomed to be crushed beneath its weight.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Countless Hellas have been sacrificed, and there have been countless people like you who take up arms—to protect, to seek vengeance, to change this cruel fate.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Hella understood this. That is why she chose to stand with them. And you... you raised her to be so compassionate. Surely, then, you must also understand—

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Behind BR-005 is no mere Apostle or calamity. It is the weight of conviction, a desperate plea for change.

steps.speaker: Shadow's Voice
steps.content: ...Get away... Get away...
A desperate plea for change...
Our spymaster warned me about you. Said you're a real expert at getting inside people's heads, making them doubt everything.
You must've run the same routine on others that you just tried on me. I bet those poor souls actually bought it, too.
But you did clear one thing up for me... so thanks for that, you bastard of Fraser and the Underground.
When Hella comes back, I'll settle all of it with you.
[Scene change] As you exit the hospital room, you find Schorl waiting for you.

steps.speaker: Option
options: I held back. I didn't lay a finger on him.

steps.content: So, does that help our trust level?

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Yes. Your restraint was commendable. Has this clarified your earlier concerns?
Not really, but... it's enough to know what I need to do next.
To start, you need to meet someone...
Just as the controversy surrounding the mobilization order reaches a fever pitch, Max King reactivates his long-dormant social media account.
Without any buildup, a single post bearing his unmistakable style instantly ignites the entire internet.

<color=#8dcdda>@MK_Max King:</color>
Alright, DisCity, let's talk. Straight talk.
I get it. The anxiety, the confusion, and even the anger. I feel it too. We're all just people, and nobody gets to sit out the storm.
Tomorrow, we vote on the Mobilization Order. Round two. This isn't just about the military; this is a historic choice for EVERY single DisCitizen.
But here's the truth, my friends. This is OUR turning point! This is the moment our city-state stands UNITED and leaps toward the future!

Let me be clear: DisCity's fate doesn't rest only with soldiers on the front line. It rests on YOUR will. On MY will. On EVERYONE'S!
War isn't some lone-hero adventure. It's a choice made by every citizen. It's US, together, unleashing strength we didn't even know we had.
Maybe you're just someone from Eastside. A shop owner in West District. A researcher buried in Nirvana's lab.
But since when are heroes only the ones holding guns on the battlefield? You can do MORE than you think!

Remember this: Every action. Every word of support. Every bit of effort—it ALL pushes this city forward.
Don't just watch from the sidelines. This era needs your voice. Your passion. Your responsibility. WE are DisCity. We don't WAIT for miracles—WE MAKE THEM.

I'm not stopping. I'm keeping this conversation going, and I'll keep moving forward. Tomorrow, you can find me on Third Avenue, Sixth District, and Fifth Avenue. If you've got concerns, opinions, big ideas? Come tell me. Don't hold back. As your Speaker, I promise you: I will LISTEN to every voice as we move forward. Together! #MobilizationOrder #ProtectOurCity #GiveYourAll #ThisIsOurFuture

The <color=#fb9259>Clown Speaker</color> is on his soapbox again. <size=28>Who actually</size> buys what he's selling?
Let's be real, that <size=45>mobilization order</size> is just about <color=#fb9259><size=52>propping up the military</color></size>. Nothing more.
The city-state already made a deal with <color=#fb9259><size=45>Augustus</color></size>. <size=28>The mobilization order is just trading power for life</size>.
If <color=#fb9259>Max King</color> had any real power, would he be doing cringe parades in the streets every day? <size=52>lol</size>

<size=28>Does he even read the </size><color=#fb9259>mobilization order</color> he's talking about? I could do a better job than this guy.
<color=#fb9259><size=52>That stupid Max King</color></size> is at it again, posting like he's the chosen one, but we all know the real deals happen behind closed doors.
Give it up, man. Everyone knows you're just a figurehead. <color=#fb9259><size=45>Augustus</color></size> is the real deal.
Selyna wakes to the sound of familiar footsteps.

steps.speaker: Selyna
steps.content: ...@#%*. (Here she comes again.)
But she feels neither anger nor panic.
It's the silver-haired girl again, back for what must be the dozenth visit. After an absence of several days, Selyna notes the fresh wounds that litter her skin.

Not that Selyna cares, of course. A warrior's instinct is to observe. It's just that she'd been the same age when she enlisted. It's just that she sees a hauntingly familiar fire in the girl's eyes...

But this time, instead of timid kindness, Selyna is met by the cold gleam of a gun barrel. A bullet whips past, grazing her hair. She should mock the girl's pathetic aim, but an inexplicable rage ignites within her instead.

steps.speaker: Selyna
steps.content: You fooled me!

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: It's you who lied!

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: @#¥@¥! (It's you who lied!!)

steps.speaker: Selyna
steps.content: You're...?!
The girl calls out in nearly flawless Outland language, revealing a traditional Furor beaded bracelet dangling from her wrist.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: Do you recognize it? It was my mother's. She was an Outlander. She taught me her language in secret. I remember every word.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: %@@¥#¥@@%#...,¥%#&@#@%@#@# (Do you recognize it? It was my mother's. She was an Outlander. She taught me her language in secret. I remember every word.)

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: My Disian name... is Elvira Stewart. But my mother gave me another name, Nysa Sadikur, to honor her family in Furor.
She raises her gun, head bowed, her entire body trembling as if suppressing a storm of rage. Finally, she lifts her gaze and, with every fiber of her being, cries out—

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: I know about the Furor Black Ring! I know you betrayed my mother! After what you did... how can you even say words like "justice"?

steps.speaker: Selyna
steps.content: What did you say?
[Black Screen]
Elvira lied. Timid by nature, she nonetheless possesses a surprising talent for performance when the situation demands.
And now, she has decided the situation demands it.
[Alarm Blaring]

steps.speaker: Alarm
steps.content: Alert. Alert. Aurum Secretum reaction detected. Outland Sinner has escaped. Repeat, Outland Sinner has escaped—

steps.speaker: Selyna
steps.content: ...@#¥@#¥ (Damn it!! Damn it all!!!)
Selyna turns and flees. Elvira doesn't pursue; instead, she sinks to her knees, her breath coming in ragged gasps.

steps.speaker: West District Staff Member
steps.content: Miss Stewart! Are you all right?!

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: I... I'm fine...
Immediately after, she activates a secret communication channel.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: Hello... it's me. The Outlander has left, and no one else noticed. Everything's under control.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: As we agreed, keep a close watch on her. Don't miss any opportunity.

More gunshots crack the air. Selyna twists aside just as one round strikes true, shattering her restraint. Behind her stands only the DisCity girl, her gun wavering wildly. She is no threat; Selyna could snap her neck and vanish before the echo of the shot fades.
But she doesn't look back.
